top_stories.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns, succession and stock impact in focus
points: Jensen Huang's immediate resignation as Nvidia CEO sent NVDA shares down 12.8% for the week, an S&P 500 top loser despite the broader market rally.
Co-founder Chris Malachowsky is reportedly being considered as a potential successor amid recent scandals.
Semiconductor and AI-adjacent peers rallied sharply as attention rotated away from Nvidia: AMD +18.9%, Broadcom +18.2%, Monolithic Power +16.8%, Arista Networks +15.5%.
The leadership transition raises questions about operational continuity at a company central to AI infrastructure buildout.

unique_angles.point: Chris Malachowsky is being floated as a potential successor to Huang amid recent scandals.

top_stories.title: Inflation data and rising Treasury yields keep Fed rate hikes in play
points: October CPI (Consumer Price Index, a measure of inflation) rose 0.4% month-over-month, beating the 0.3% consensus forecast and signaling persistent price pressures.
Markets now price in a possible 50-basis-point (0.5 percentage point) December rate hike, up from expectations of just 25 basis points (0.25 percentage points).
10-year Treasury bond yield jumped 26 basis points to 5.14%, later hitting its highest level since October on hot wholesale price data.
Hotter-than-expected wholesale prices add to inflation concerns, reinforcing the case for continued Fed tightening despite earlier hopes for cuts.

unique_angles.point: Friday's market reaction included S&P 500 down 0.4% and Nasdaq down 0.9%, while the Dow still gained 0.1%, reflecting mixed sensitivity to the yield move.
Despite rate concerns, major indices still posted solid weekly gains: Dow +2%, S&P 500 +2.5%, Nasdaq +2.2%.

top_stories.title: Anthropic's upcoming IPO and AI ambitions
points: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon the company aims to 'underpromise and overdeliver' ahead of next week's IPO (Initial Public Offering, when a private company first sells shares to the public).
The IPO is primarily intended to secure cash for computing infrastructure rather than to maximize valuation; reports indicate the targeted valuation has dropped below earlier $2 trillion hopes.
Anthropic buys computing capacity on the 'low side' of growth projections and supplements as needed—the IPO funds provide a buffer for this strategy.
Amodei outlined ambitious AI goals including scientific breakthroughs (cancer, Alzheimer's, heart disease) and deploying AI agents in robotics and cybersecurity.

unique_angles.point: The Anthropic IPO is flagged as a key catalyst to watch this week alongside Nvidia shockwaves, a Nike event, and the GTA 6 video game launch.
Investor Bill Ackman has said he does not plan to add Anthropic to his portfolio.

items.title: Global Energy Price Divergence
points: U.S. natural gas prices hover around $3 per MMBtu (million British thermal units, a measure of gas volume) while Europe and Asia pay approximately $30 per MMBtu—a 10x gap driven by Iran-related geopolitical disruptions.
American buyers have been shielded by domestic production and LNG (liquefied natural gas) infrastructure, giving energy-intensive U.S. industries a competitive advantage.
The gap illustrates how geopolitical shocks redistribute economic stress unevenly across global markets.

items.title: SpaceX attempts historic Starship 'double catch'
points: SpaceX will attempt a first-ever 'double catch' of its Starship rocket and booster in a single mission tonight, a major test of reusable rocket technology.

items.title: Microsoft outage disrupts core productivity tools
points: Microsoft suffered a significant outage affecting email, Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for users.
The cause remains under investigation, with speculation about possible links to layoffs or AI-related changes.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: Anthropic is trying to 'underpromise and overdeliver'

headlines: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon the AI startup aims to 'underpromise and overdeliver' ahead of next week's IPO, with the company seeking additional cash for computing infrastructure rather than maximum valuation.
S&P 500 fell 0.4% and Nasdaq dropped 0.9% Friday as 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since October on hot wholesale prices, keeping Fed rate hikes in play.
SpaceX will attempt a first-ever 'double catch' of Starship and its booster tonight in a major test of its reusable rocket technology.
Microsoft experienced a major outage disrupting email, Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for users; unclear if layoffs or AI changes played a role.
Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky is being considered as a potential successor to CEO Jensen Huang amid recent scandals.

sections.title: Anthropic IPO Strategy and Capital Needs
points: Amodei told Dimon Anthropic is going public primarily to secure cash for computing infrastructure, describing it as the company's 'deepest business dilemma.'
The startup buys computing capacity on the 'low side' of what growth projections justify, then supplements when demand exceeds expectations—the IPO provides financial buffer for this strategy.
Amodei emphasized Anthropic wants to underpromise and overdeliver rather than pursue the highest possible IPO valuation.

The CEO laid out ambitious visions for AI in scientific discovery (cancer, Alzheimer's, heart disease treatments) and deploying AI agents in robotics and cybersecurity, noting exponential gains in cognition create new market opportunities.

sections.title: Market Moves and Inflation Signals
points: 10-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since October Friday, driven by hotter-than-expected wholesale price data.
The rise in yields keeps Federal Reserve rate hikes in play despite expectations for potential cuts, signaling persistent inflation concerns.
S&P 500 closed down 0.4%, Nasdaq down 0.9%, while Dow gained 0.1% on Friday.
